name: GPT-1
positioning: First to show that unsupervised pre-training plus fine-tuning boosts NLP task performance — the original generative pre-trained transformer that started the GPT line.

name: BERT
positioning: First to show bidirectional transformer pretraining at scale — BERT-Large set SOTA on 11 NLP benchmarks at once and kicked off the pretrained-encoder era that every later model in this timeline builds on.

name: GPT-2
positioning: Scaled GPT-1's recipe up to 1.5B parameters and became the first model withheld as 'too dangerous to release', with full weights only coming out after a staged disclosure — OpenAI's first open-weights release in this line.
hype: Announced Feb 2019 as 'too dangerous to release'; the full weights only followed in Nov 2019 after a staged-release controversy.

name: GPT-3
positioning: Scaled GPT-2's 1.5B parameters to 175B and pulled the weights back behind a closed API — first made publicly accessible via the OpenAI API on 2020-06-11, kick-starting the LLM API ecosystem.

name: ChatGPT
positioning: Displaced the developer-only GPT-3 API with a free conversational interface built on GPT-3.5 — the first OpenAI model product aimed at everyone, not just API customers.
hype: Reached ~1M users in 5 days, triggering the mainstream LLM wave.

name: Claude 1
positioning: Anthropic's first public model and first to market a 100K-token context window, arriving via Slack and API access rather than a consumer app.
hype: Its release landed on the exact same day as GPT-4 — Anthropic's debut was instantly measured against the model that defined 2023.

name: GPT-4
positioning: First flagship LLM to accept image inputs, and a step-change in capability over GPT-3.5 — passing the bar exam at ~90th percentile.

name: Claude 2
positioning: Displaced Claude 1 with stronger coding and reasoning scores and launched claude.ai, Anthropic's first consumer-facing chat app, taking the fight to consumer chatbots' home turf.

name: Llama 2
positioning: Meta's first commercially usable open-weights LLM — free for most commercial use and downloadable same day with Microsoft, it displaced the research-only open-weights status quo.

name: Mistral 7B
positioning: Displaced Llama 2 13B as the go-to small open model — the best 7B of its time, it even neared Llama 34B while shipping Apache 2.0 weights.

name: Grok-1
positioning: xAI's first model, gated to X Premium+ subscribers at launch. Its 314B-param MoE weights were open-sourced months later (2024-03-17) — the lab's first weights release.

name: GPT-4 Turbo
positioning: Quadrupled GPT-4's 32k context window to 128k tokens, added vision, and crashed the price by 3x.

name: Gemini 1.0
positioning: Google's first natively multimodal frontier family — Ultra outperformed GPT-4 on most major benchmarks, while Pro/Nano tiers reached Bard and Pixel devices at launch.
hype: Google admitted its launch demo video was edited rather than a real-time interaction, drawing criticism for overstaging what Gemini could actually do.

name: Mixtral 8x7B
positioning: First high-quality openly licensed sparse MoE — activating only 13B of 47B parameters, it matched or beat GPT-3.5 and Llama 2 70B and displaced Mistral 7B as the open-weights value pick.

name: Gemini 1.5 Pro
positioning: First frontier model with a widely noted 1M-token context window — a leap of orders of magnitude over Gemini 1.0, paired with MoE architecture, first shown in limited preview with GA in May 2024.

name: Mistral Large
positioning: Mistral's first closed, API-only frontier model — a reversal of its open-weights identity (Mixtral was still the last open flagship), positioned for coding.
hype: Launched the same day as Mistral's $415M Series B and the Le Chat assistant, turning the release into a business-model story about the open-weights champion going closed.

name: Claude 3
positioning: Its Opus tier became the first model to beat GPT-4 on several benchmarks, breaking OpenAI's hold on the flagship lane, with a 200K context and vision input.

name: Grok-1.5
positioning: Displaced Grok-1 with improved reasoning and a 128k-token context window — xAI's first major context jump.

name: Llama 3
positioning: Displaced Llama 2 across the board — trained on 15T tokens, the 70B beat Gemini Pro 1.5 and Claude 3 Sonnet on most benchmarks while staying open-weights, and launched alongside the Meta AI assistant on Facebook and WhatsApp.

name: DeepSeek-V2
positioning: Crashed the price of inference in China: multi-head latent attention plus MoE slashed output cost to ~2 RMB per million tokens, a price level that displaced incumbents' pricing across the market.
hype: Its launch triggered China's LLM price war.

name: GPT-4o
positioning: First 'omni' flagship natively handling text, audio, and vision in one model — ~2x the speed and half the price of GPT-4 Turbo, with free-tier access.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet
positioning: A mid-size model that displaced Anthropic's own flagship — outperforming Claude 3 Opus on coding and reasoning at Sonnet price — defining the cost-efficiency frontier of mid-2024.

name: Llama 3.1 405B
positioning: First openly downloadable frontier-class model — the 405B was competitive with GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet, something no prior open release achieved, and stretched Llama 3's context to 128K.

name: Grok-2
positioning: Displaced Grok-1.5 as xAI's frontier, matching frontier-2024 quality; image generation (Dec 2024) and an API beta (2024-11-04) followed within months.

name: o1-preview
positioning: Opened the test-time-compute reasoning lane: first broadly available reasoning model, solving 83% of AIME qualifiers where GPT-4o managed ~13%.

name: Qwen2.5
positioning: Open-weights family trained on 18T tokens that quickly became the world's most fine-tuned open model base.

name: Claude 3.5 Sonnet v2
positioning: First to ship 'computer use' — a public beta of general screen, keyboard and mouse control — turning the mid-tier Sonnet into a leading agentic coding model.
hype: The computer-use beta was the release's signature moment: a model operating a computer like a human user.

name: QwQ-32B-Preview
positioning: First to bring o1-style reasoning to Apache 2.0 open weights — and it beat o1 itself on some math benchmarks at release.

name: Gemini 2.0 Flash
positioning: First Gemini 2.0 model, framing Google's 'agentic era' — beat 1.5 Pro on key benchmarks at 2x speed and crashed the price of that tier by opening it to all Gemini users on day one.

name: DeepSeek-V3
positioning: Scaled the V2 recipe into a 671B-param MoE that matched GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet on many benchmarks — for a reported ~$5.6M in GPU-hours.
hype: The reported ~$5.6M training bill for a model matching GPT-4o and Claude 3.5 Sonnet became the release's dominant storyline.

name: DeepSeek-R1
positioning: Matched o1-class reasoning and shipped it MIT-licensed — the first open-weights model to reach that class, displacing the assumption that frontier reasoning stays closed.
hype: Its free app overtook ChatGPT at #1 on the US iOS App Store (Jan 27), and the fallout triggered an 18% Nvidia share drop.

name: Grok 3
positioning: Displaced Grok 2 as xAI's flagship, trained on the Colossus cluster and branded 'The Age of Reasoning Agents' — xAI's entry into the reasoning-model wave QwQ and R1 had opened.

name: Claude 3.7 Sonnet
positioning: First hybrid reasoning model, letting users toggle extended thinking within one model instead of choosing between separate reasoning and chat models, while topping agentic coding benchmarks at release.

name: GPT-4.5
positioning: OpenAI's largest 'classic' pre-trained model, with better world knowledge and EQ — but a dead end in the line, superseded by GPT-5 months later as the reasoning era took over.

name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
positioning: First Gemini with built-in 'thinking' via a controllable reasoning budget, plus a 1M-token context — displaced the Gemini 2.0 generation as Google's flagship.
hype: Debuted at #1 on the LMArena leaderboard on release.

name: Llama 4
positioning: Meta's first natively multimodal MoE Llama generation — but the launch flopped because the LMArena benchmark controversy over an unreleased experimental variant marred it.
hype: Benchmark controversy: LMArena scores came from an unreleased experimental variant rather than the shipped Llama 4 model, marring the launch.

name: o3
positioning: Displaced o1 as the reasoning flagship and became the first model to pass Codeforces at elite (2727 Elo) level; announced at '12 Days of Shipmas' in Dec 2024 and publicly released with o4-mini on 2025-04-16.

name: Qwen3
positioning: Doubled Qwen2.5's 18T training tokens to 36T and made thinking/non-thinking modes switchable inside one Apache 2.0 family spanning 0.6B to 235B-A22B across 119 languages.

name: Mistral Medium 3
positioning: Crashed the price of frontier-class multimodal — near-Mistral-Large performance at roughly 1/8 the cost, positioned for coding and STEM enterprise workloads.

name: Claude 4
positioning: Opus 4 set a new SOTA on SWE-bench (~72.5%), extending the agentic coding lead Claude 3.7 Sonnet had taken, while Sonnet 4 shipped Claude Code to GA — a step change in long-horizon agentic coding.

name: Grok 4
positioning: Displaced Grok 3 with xAI's first native tool use plus real-time search, adding a SuperGrok Heavy multi-agent tier for the top end.

name: Kimi K2
positioning: First open-weights agentic flagship to match frontier closed models — a 1T-param MoE with 32B active parameters, at a fraction of rivals' cost.

name: GLM-4.5
positioning: Followed Kimi K2 into the open agentic-MoE field with a 355B-A32B MIT-licensed hybrid reasoning/agentic model, topping open-model agentic benchmarks and shipping FP8 weights.

name: GPT-5
positioning: Collapsed the separate reasoning lane back into the flagship: a unified system with a built-in reasoning router, shipped to all ChatGPT users (incl. free tier) on launch day with a ~45% drop in hallucinations vs GPT-4o.

name: Qwen3-Max
positioning: Alibaba's first trillion-parameter flagship — and a break from its open-weights streak: proprietary, API-only, with GA thinking mode on Sep 24 after a Sep 5 preview.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.5
positioning: Raised the family's SWE-bench Verified SOTA from Claude 4's ~72.5% to ~77.2% and sustained autonomous focus for 30+ hours on long tasks, adding memory and context-editing features.

name: Kimi K2 Thinking
positioning: Extended Kimi K2's agentic base with a dedicated long-horizon reasoning and tool-use mode, kept open-weights.

name: GPT-5.1
positioning: Adaptive-reasoning successor to GPT-5, rolled out in ChatGPT on 2025-11-12 with API access announced the following day.

name: Grok 4.1
positioning: Displaced Grok 4 as xAI's late-2025 flagship, later joined by a Fast variant and agent tooling — and itself superseded by Grok 4.20 in Feb 2026.

name: Gemini 3 Pro
positioning: Third-generation flagship that displaced Gemini 2.5 Pro atop Google's lineup, shipping in the Gemini app on day one rather than a staged rollout.
hype: Launched at #1 across major reasoning and coding leaderboards.

name: Claude Opus 4.5
positioning: Frontier Opus that displaced the ~77.2% SWE-bench Verified mark set by Sonnet 4.5, pushing it to ~80.9% while cutting prices aggressively and introducing effort-based control and strong computer use.

name: DeepSeek-V3.2
positioning: Brought thinking during tool use to DeepSeek's open-weights flagship line, holding the general-flagship slot until the V4 Preview in April 2026.

name: Mistral Large 3
positioning: Displaced Mistral Medium 3 as flagship — and reversed the original Mistral Large's closed turn, returning the Large line (mistral-large-2512) to open weights alongside Ministral 3.

name: GPT-5.2
positioning: First model to beat or tie human experts on GDPval (70.9%), plus 80% SWE-bench Verified and 52.9% ARC-AGI-2 — a broad frontier sweep in one release, stepping up from mid-tier GPT-5.1.

name: Gemini 3 Flash
positioning: Extended the Gemini 3 generation down from 3 Pro — the faster everyday/developer workhorse of the same generation, trading Pro-tier depth for speed and reach.

name: Kimi K2.5
positioning: Succeeded the K2 Thinking lineage by folding visual input, reasoning, coding and agent modes — including an Agent Swarm preview — into one general Kimi model.

name: Claude Opus 4.6
positioning: Extended the Opus line's context from Claude 3's 200K to a beta 1M window while adding stronger planning and code review on top of Opus 4.5's frontier coding.
hype: Kicked off a rapid 4.x refresh cadence, with Sonnet 4.6 following on Feb 17.

name: GPT-5.3-Codex
positioning: Traded GPT-5.2's broad frontier sweep for a focused lane: an agentic coding model for professional software work, with the ultra-fast real-time Codex-Spark variant following Feb 12.

name: Qwen3.5
positioning: Brought native multimodality (text/image/video) into the main open-weight Qwen family for the first time, starting with Qwen3.5-397B-A17B.

name: Grok 4.20
positioning: Displaced Grok 4.1 with a 4-agent multi-agent architecture and a 2M-token context window — the largest context in this timeline.

name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
positioning: Broad-spectrum refresh following Opus 4.6's planning and code-review gains, extending the upgrade across coding, computer use, long-context reasoning and agent planning.

name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
positioning: Became Google's Pro-tier flagship for complex reasoning and agent tasks over 3.1 predecessors' Flash-tier sibling — and held the top-Pro spot until the 3.5/3.8-era releases displaced it.

name: GPT-5.4
positioning: Folded GPT-5.3-Codex's coding focus back into a general model: unified Thinking/Pro reasoning, coding, and agentic workflows, with mini/nano variants following Mar 17.

name: Muse Spark
positioning: First Meta Superintelligence Labs model — displaced the Llama line as Meta's public flagship with natively multimodal reasoning, tool use, and multi-agent 'Contemplating' mode, available at meta.ai with a private API preview.
hype: Marked Meta's pivot away from open weights — its first closed frontier release after the open Llama line.

name: Claude Opus 4.7
positioning: Broadened the Opus line beyond 4.6's planning and code-review focus to high-resolution vision and advanced software engineering, positioned as the bridge into the Claude 5 generation.

name: GPT-5.5
positioning: Stepped back up to flagship for complex coding, research, and data-analysis work, positioned for agentic long-horizon tasks beyond mid-tier GPT-5.4; shipped with a system card on 2026-04-23.

name: DeepSeek-V4
positioning: Displaced V3.2 as DeepSeek's flagship, previewing V4-Flash/V4-Pro under MIT with 1M-token context; official releases followed Jul 31 and Aug 13, 2026.

name: Mistral Medium 3.5
positioning: Displaced Mistral Medium 3 as Mistral's flagship-grade general/multimodal release in April 2026, after Mistral Small 4 had shipped in March.

name: Grok 4.3
positioning: Displaced Grok 4.20 Beta as the consumer flagship with 1M context, native video input and document output, priced at $1.25/$2.50 per M tokens.

name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
positioning: Outperformed Gemini 3.1 Pro on agentic/coding benchmarks at Flash-tier speed — displacing the Pro from the default seat in the Gemini app and AI Mode while kicking off the 3.5 series (3.5 Pro slated later).
hype: Headlined Google I/O 2026 as the new default model for the Gemini app and AI Mode.

name: Qwen3.7-Max
positioning: Displaced Qwen3-Max as Alibaba's proprietary flagship, repositioned for the agent era of long-running autonomous workflows, with Plus/visual snapshot variants following in June.

name: Claude Opus 4.8
positioning: Closed out the 4.x line holding the #1 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (61.4) among peers, the last Opus standing before the Claude 5 generation.
hype: The final 4.x Opus — capping a rapid run of point releases ahead of the generation change.

name: Claude Fable 5
positioning: First generally available Mythos-class Claude, opening the 2026 generation change from the 4.x line, with the stronger Mythos 5 held back under restricted trusted access.
hype: The staged release — Fable 5 for everyone, Mythos 5 gated behind 'trusted access' — made access tiers the story of the launch.

name: Claude Sonnet 5
positioning: Reset the price floor of the new generation's mid lane, shipping as the low-cost agentic workhorse at a permanent $2/$10 per M tokens against the pricier Fable-class flagships.

name: GPT-5.6
positioning: Crashed the intelligence-per-dollar curve: marketed as 'frontier intelligence that scales' with markedly better value than GPT-5.5, split into a Sol variant in ChatGPT and a Luna variant for free/API users.

name: Kimi K3
positioning: Scaled the Kimi line from K2's 1T to a 2.8T-parameter flagship with native vision and 1M context, debuting the Kimi Delta Attention architecture — hosted Jul 16, full weights Jul 27.

name: Grok 4.5
positioning: Displaced Grok 4.3 as xAI's smartest model at launch, trained alongside Cursor and claiming ~4.2x token efficiency vs Opus 4.8 on SWE Bench Pro at $2/$6 per M tokens.

name: Claude Opus 5
positioning: Displaced Fable-5-class pricing — near-frontier intelligence at half the price — as the new default on Claude Max, with SOTA on Frontier-Bench and GDPval-AA.

name: Qwen3.8-Max
positioning: Displaced Qwen3.7-Max and answered Kimi K3's 2.8T flagship with a 2.4T-param sparse MoE (~95B active) and 1M-token context — returning Alibaba's top tier to open weights (Aug 12) after the proprietary Max era.

name: Grok 4.6
positioning: Landed two weeks after Grok 4.5 and matched GPT-5.6 Sol on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (61), making back-to-back frontier cadence the xAI story.

name: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next
positioning: First architecture preview of Qwen4: an open multimodal MoE (125B total, 6B active) introducing Qwen Sparse Attention as the efficiency-focused counterpart to Qwen3.8-Max.

name: Claude Fable 5.1
positioning: Anthropic's most advanced model line to date, displacing Fable 5 with large gains in agentic scientific research (52.6% Terminal-Bench-Science) and coding, while keeping the one-model, two-safeguard-levels split.

name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
positioning: The Flash line's step past 3.5 — a long-horizon engineering/agent model at $0.75/$3.75 intro pricing per million tokens, plus a restricted Flash Cyber variant for trusted defenders.

name: Muse Spark 1.3
positioning: Iterated past Muse Spark — roughly 20% fewer tool calls than 1.2 on long-horizon agentic/coding work, while Meta kept an open-weight flank via the Apache 2.0 Muse Glimmer 30B shipped in August.

name: GPT-6 Astra
positioning: Displaced GPT-5.6 as OpenAI's most capable broadly deployed model, and the first to reach the 'Critical' cybersecurity level under the Preparedness Framework.
